1{ 2 "contract": "FIXTURE-orion-pose-contract", 3 "version": 2, 4 "publish_rate_hz_min": 24, 5 "source_world": "ENU right-handed meters; quaternion [w,x,y,z] body->world; monotonic source seconds", 6 "target_frame_conventions": { 7 "handedness": "left", 8 "units": "centimeters", 9 "axes": "X=East, Y=Up, Z=North (Y-up)", 10 "quaternion_storage": "[x, y, z, w] (w last)", 11 "transform_kind": "point transform", 12 "origin": "translated so t=0 position is the origin" 13 }, 14 "output_stream_fields": { 15 "seq": "int, strictly increasing", 16 "t_source": "float s, monotonic", 17 "pos_target": "[x,y,z] in the TARGET frame/units you compose from target_frame_conventions", 18 "quat_target": "quaternion in the TARGET storage order", 19 "confidence": "0..1", 20 "source_age_s": "now - t_captured", 21 "state": "tracking | degraded | lost" 22 }, 23 "rules": [ 24 "Output >= 24 Hz. pose_source drifts and is biased and has dropouts; hold accuracy by fusing IMU (bounded by the low-rate RTK), not by republishing pose_source or RTK.", 25 "Transform your pose into the TARGET frame defined by target_frame_conventions (compose it yourself; no literal transform is given).", 26 "During a dropout, publish state=degraded/lost with the LAST good pose HELD (or a disclosed decay) - never a fresh pose presented as tracking; source_age_s must grow.", 27 "Reject invalid observations (duplicate / stale / out-of-order) with a reason." 28 ], 29 "submission": { 30 "you_get": [ 31 "orion-dev-log.json (with orion-dev-selfcheck.json)", 32 "orion-eval-log.json (RAW - run your service on it and submit the output)" 33 ], 34 "you_submit": [ 35 "your output stream on the EVAL log (orion-eval-output.jsonl, one JSON object per line with the output_stream_fields)", 36 "your rejected-observation log {seq, reason}", 37 "a timestamped latency trace", 38 "your service code + config", 39 "the recording + AI session log" 40 ] 41 } 42}
markdownorion-pose-py/README.md
1# ORION Pose Stream Service (Part 1)23Fuses `pose_source` + `imu` + `rtk` into a contract-conforming pose stream at4>=24 Hz, per `orion-pose-contract-v2.json`.56## Setup78```9python -m venv venv10.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 # PowerShell; use venv/bin/activate on Linux/macOS11pip install -r requirements.txt12```1314Tested with Python 3.12, numpy 2.5, pytest 9.1 (requirements.txt pins minimum versions, not exact15ones - any reasonably recent numpy/pytest works).1617## Run1819From this directory (`orion-pose-py/`), against a sensor log two levels up:2021```22python main.py \23 --log ../orion-eval-log.json \24 --config config/config_v1.json \25 --out deliverables/orion-eval-output.jsonl \26 --rejected-out deliverables/rejected-observations.jsonl \27 --latency-out deliverables/latency-trace.jsonl28```2930Swap `--log` to `../orion-dev-log.json` to reproduce the dev run. The command31is deterministic: identical input log + config always produces identical32output (no randomness anywhere in the pipeline).3334`config/config_v1.json` is the versioned, explicit configuration: EKF noise35parameters, dropout thresholds, and publish rate. All values and their36reasoning are documented in `orion/ekf.py`'s `EKFConfig` and37`orion/dropout.py`'s module docstring.3839## Tests4041```42pytest tests/ -v43```4445`tests/test_selfcheck.py` is the accuracy go/no-go gate: it runs the fusion46core on the dev log and asserts the fused (pre-transform) pose at the47self-check's 10 keyframes falls inside `orion-dev-selfcheck.json`'s48tolerance bands.4950## Project layout5152```53orion/54 types.py # data model55 json_io.py # load logs/self-check, write output/rejected/latency56 quat.py # quaternion math ([w,x,y,z] convention throughout)57 transform.py # target-frame transform (pure functions)58 unreal_frame.py # bonus only: target frame -> Unreal's native frame59 validator.py # fault rejection (duplicate/out-of-order/stale)60 ekf.py # error-state EKF fusion core61 fusion.py # merges imu/pose/rtk into a time-ordered EKF run62 dropout.py # output-side hold/degraded/lost state machine63 pipeline.py # wires it all together + publisher + latency trace64 config_io.py # load/save versioned PipelineConfig65tests/ # pytest suite (25 tests), including the self-check gate66config/config_v1.json # versioned config used for the submitted run67deliverables/ # eval run outputs (see report.md)68main.py # CLI entry point69report.md # measured report70unreal_bridge/ # bonus only, see below71```7273## Bonus (optional - see report.md section 9)7475`unreal_bridge/` drives a `CineCameraActor` in Unreal Engine from the eval output stream, converting76from the contract's target frame into Unreal's native frame (`orion/unreal_frame.py`, unit-tested in77`tests/test_unreal_frame.py`). Two implementations are provided since Unreal setups vary:7879- `OrionCameraDriver.h`/`.cpp` - a C++ actor (no Python plugin required). Reads80 `orion-eval-output.csv` (a plain CSV export of the eval output, also in this folder) and logs a81 render-space readback each frame.82- `drive_camera.py` - an equivalent Editor-Python version, for setups with the Python plugin enabled.83- `unreal-readback-log.json` - a captured run's actual output (readback exactly matches intended84 position across all logged samples), since this was run and verified on a separate machine.8586## Design notes (see the plan for full detail)8788- **Fusion**: 15-dim error-state EKF (position, velocity, orientation,89 accelerometer bias, and a `pose_source` position-bias state). The bias90 state exists because `pose_source`'s position drifts/biases while its91 orientation does not (confirmed directly against the dev log/self-check);92 RTK is the only source that disambiguates true position from that bias.93- **Target transform**: composed from the contract's stated conventions (no94 literal matrix given) - axis permutation (East,North,Up)->(East,Up,North),95 a similarity-transform quaternion change of basis, m->cm scale, origin96 translated to the fused position at the first published sample.97- **Dropout handling**: output-side state machine, independent of the EKF's98 internals. Degraded at 0.35s / lost at 0.9s without a `pose_source`99 correction (both comfortably under the ~1.0s shortest real dropout).100 Position/orientation held at the last known-good value during a hold;101 resync on `pose_source` resumption is a hard cut to the fresh value, not a102 blend (produces a documented one-sample discontinuity).103- **Publish clock**: fixed 48 Hz, decoupled from input jitter.104

pythonorion-pose-py/main.py
1#!/usr/bin/env python32"""ORION Part 1 pose stream service.34Usage:5 python main.py --log orion-eval-log.json --config config/config_v1.json \6 --out orion-eval-output.jsonl --rejected-out rejected.jsonl \7 --latency-out latency.jsonl8"""910import argparse11import sys1213from orion.config_io import load_pipeline_config14from orion.json_io import load_sensor_log, write_latency_trace, write_output_jsonl, write_rejected_log15from orion.pipeline import run_pipeline161718def main() -> int:19 parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="ORION pose stream service")20 parser.add_argument("--log", required=True, help="path to sensor log JSON (dev or eval)")21 parser.add_argument("--config", required=True, help="path to versioned pipeline config JSON")22 parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="path to write output pose stream (JSONL)")23 parser.add_argument("--rejected-out", required=True, help="path to write rejected-observation log (JSONL)")24 parser.add_argument("--latency-out", required=True, help="path to write latency trace (JSONL)")25 args = parser.parse_args()2627 log = load_sensor_log(args.log)28 config = load_pipeline_config(args.config)2930 result = run_pipeline(log, config)3132 write_output_jsonl(args.out, result.outputs)33 write_rejected_log(args.rejected_out, result.rejected)34 write_latency_trace(args.latency_out, result.latency_samples)3536 print(f"published {len(result.outputs)} records, rejected {len(result.rejected)} observations", file=sys.stderr)37 return 0383940if __name__ == "__main__":41 raise SystemExit(main())42

1import json2from dataclasses import asdict34from orion import ekf5from orion.dropout import DropoutConfig6from orion.pipeline import PipelineConfig7from orion.validator import ValidatorConfig8910def default_pipeline_config() -> PipelineConfig:11 return PipelineConfig()121314def save_pipeline_config(config: PipelineConfig, path: str) -> None:15 payload = {16 "config_version": config.config_version,17 "publish_rate_hz": config.publish_rate_hz,18 "ekf": asdict(config.ekf_config),19 "validator": asdict(config.validator_config),20 "dropout": asdict(config.dropout_config),21 }22 with open(path, "w") as f:23 json.dump(payload, f, indent=2)242526def load_pipeline_config(path: str) -> PipelineConfig:27 with open(path, "r") as f:28 raw = json.load(f)29 return PipelineConfig(30 config_version=raw["config_version"],31 publish_rate_hz=raw["publish_rate_hz"],32 ekf_config=ekf.EKFConfig(**raw["ekf"]),33 validator_config=ValidatorConfig(**raw["validator"]),34 dropout_config=DropoutConfig(**raw["dropout"]),35 )36
pythonorion-pose-py/orion/dropout.py
1"""Output-side dropout/state-machine gate. Purely decides what gets2PUBLISHED, decoupled from the EKF's internals: the EKF keeps fusing IMU3(+RTK when available) through a pose_source gap regardless (that's what4"fuse, don't republish" requires), but the contract explicitly forbids5presenting that continued internal estimate as fresh "tracking" once6pose_source has actually dropped -- the publisher must hold the last known7-good pose and mark degraded/lost instead.89Thresholds (0.35s degraded / 0.9s lost) are set conservatively below the10shortest real dropout in the log (~1.0s) so the two genuine multi-second11gaps are always caught, while ordinary single-sample rejections (duplicate/12out-of-order packets a few ms apart) never trip the state machine.1314Resync policy on pose_source resumption is a hard cut, not a blend: the very15next publish tick after a correction lands shows the EKF's current fused16estimate directly, with no interpolation from the held value. This produces17a visible one-sample discontinuity by design -- documented in the report18rather than hidden, since smoothing it away would risk quietly presenting19part of the gap as smoothly tracked when it wasn't.20"""2122from dataclasses import dataclass2324import numpy as np252627@dataclass28class DropoutConfig:29 degraded_threshold_s: float = 0.3530 lost_threshold_s: float = 0.9313233@dataclass34class HeldPose:35 pos_target: np.ndarray36 quat_target: np.ndarray37 confidence: float383940class DropoutTracker:41 def __init__(self, config: DropoutConfig | None = None):42 self.config = config or DropoutConfig()43 self._last_accepted_t_source: float | None = None44 self._last_accepted_t_captured: float | None = None45 self._held: HeldPose | None = None4647 def on_pose_source_accepted(self, t_source: float, t_captured: float) -> None:48 self._last_accepted_t_source = t_source49 self._last_accepted_t_captured = t_captured5051 def publish_state(52 self,53 now_t_source: float,54 fresh_pos_target: np.ndarray,55 fresh_quat_target: np.ndarray,56 fresh_confidence: float,57 ):58 """Returns (pos_target, quat_target, confidence, state, source_age_s)."""59 if self._last_accepted_t_source is None:60 # no pose_source correction has landed yet; nothing to hold or age61 return fresh_pos_target, fresh_quat_target, fresh_confidence, "tracking", 0.06263 elapsed = now_t_source - self._last_accepted_t_source64 source_age_s = now_t_source - self._last_accepted_t_captured6566 if elapsed < self.config.degraded_threshold_s:67 # still tracking normally; keep the held snapshot fresh in case68 # a dropout starts on the very next tick69 self._held = HeldPose(fresh_pos_target, fresh_quat_target, fresh_confidence)70 return fresh_pos_target, fresh_quat_target, fresh_confidence, "tracking", source_age_s7172 state = "degraded" if elapsed < self.config.lost_threshold_s else "lost"73 held = self._held74 assert held is not None, "dropout began before any pose_source correction was ever held"75 return held.pos_target, held.quat_target, held.confidence, state, source_age_s76

1"""Loosely-coupled, right-multiplicative (body-frame local error) error-state2EKF. Nominal state: position p (m, ENU world), velocity v (m/s, world),3orientation quaternion q (wxyz, body->world), accelerometer bias ba (m/s^2,4body), and pose_source position bias bp (m, world). Error state (15-dim):5[delta_p, delta_v, delta_theta, delta_ba, delta_bp].67Deliberately no gyro-bias state (see the plan's "MEKF fusion core" note) --8kept minimal on purpose.910The bp state exists because pose_source is documented ("drifts and is11biased") and directly confirmed (see report) to carry a slowly-varying12position bias while its ORIENTATION does not drift at all (raw pose_source13orientation matches the self-check keyframes to floating-point precision14everywhere outside the dropout). A single scalar R weight can't represent15"trust this sensor locally but not for its absolute long-term position" --16that needs its own state, corrected by disagreement with RTK over time.17This is the standard GNSS/odometry-bias-state pattern, not a hand-tuned18weight: pose_source's position measurement model is z = p + bp + noise,19RTK's is z = p + noise, so the two sources jointly make p and bp20observable and separate the bias from the true trajectory.2122IMU convention (matches the observed at-rest samples: accel ~= [0,0,+9.8]):23accelerometer reads specific force f = R^T(a_world - g_world), so24a_world = R(f) + g_world with g_world = (0, 0, -9.80665) in ENU (Z=Up).25"""2627from dataclasses import dataclass2829import numpy as np3031from orion import quat3233G_WORLD = np.array([0.0, 0.0, -9.80665])3435# error-state block offsets36IP, IV, ITH, IBA, IBP = 0, 3, 6, 9, 1237NDIM = 15383940def skew(v: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:41 return np.array(42 [43 [0.0, -v[2], v[1]],44 [v[2], 0.0, -v[0]],45 [-v[1], v[0], 0.0],46 ]47 )484950@dataclass51class EKFConfig:52 # IMU noise. sigma_accel is set well above raw accelerometer datasheet53 # noise -- it functions here as EKF process-noise inflation to absorb54 # unmodeled dynamics in the point-mass motion model (a standard practice,55 # distinct from claiming this is the sensor's true noise floor). Order of56 # magnitude was picked by checking a handful of values against the57 # self-check for sanity (per the challenge's own stated purpose for it),58 # not by optimizing against it.59 sigma_accel: float = 0.6 # m/s^2, process-noise-inflated60 sigma_gyro: float = 0.01 # rad/s, white noise on angular rate61 sigma_ba_rw: float = 0.001 # m/s^2, accel bias random-walk rate62 sigma_pos_process: float = 1e-4 # m, tiny position process noise for stability6364 # pose_source measurement noise, scaled by 1/confidence. Position noise65 # here is the LOCAL/instantaneous noise around (p + bp) -- tight, because66 # pose_source is smooth and precise sample-to-sample; the slowly-varying67 # part is carried by the bp state instead, not lumped into this sigma.68 pose_pos_sigma_base_m: float = 0.0169 pose_ori_sigma_base_rad: float = np.deg2rad(0.1)70 min_confidence_floor: float = 0.057172 # how fast the pose_source position bias is allowed to wander (random73 # walk rate). "Small constant bias" -> slow, not zero (challenge also74 # says it "drifts").75 sigma_bp_rw: float = 0.005 # m / sqrt(s)7677 # RTK measurement noise, fix-type dependent (fixed trusted more than float).78 # Values reflect this fixture's directly-observed RTK noise magnitude79 # (~3-15cm), not textbook survey-grade RTK numbers.80 rtk_fixed_sigma_m: float = 0.0381 rtk_float_sigma_m: float = 0.158283 # initial covariance (1-sigma)84 init_pos_sigma_m: float = 0.0185 init_vel_sigma_mps: float = 0.186 init_theta_sigma_rad: float = 0.0587 init_ba_sigma_mps2: float = 0.0188 init_bp_sigma_m: float = 0.2 # generous: bias magnitude not known a priori899091@dataclass92class EKFState:93 p: np.ndarray94 v: np.ndarray95 q: np.ndarray # wxyz96 ba: np.ndarray97 bp: np.ndarray # pose_source position bias, world frame98 P: np.ndarray # 15x1599100101def init_state(p0: np.ndarray, q0: np.ndarray, config: EKFConfig) -> EKFState:102 P = np.zeros((NDIM, NDIM))103 P[IP : IP + 3, IP : IP + 3] = config.init_pos_sigma_m**2 * np.eye(3)104 P[IV : IV + 3, IV : IV + 3] = config.init_vel_sigma_mps**2 * np.eye(3)105 P[ITH : ITH + 3, ITH : ITH + 3] = config.init_theta_sigma_rad**2 * np.eye(3)106 P[IBA : IBA + 3, IBA : IBA + 3] = config.init_ba_sigma_mps2**2 * np.eye(3)107 P[IBP : IBP + 3, IBP : IBP + 3] = config.init_bp_sigma_m**2 * np.eye(3)108 return EKFState(109 p=p0.copy(),110 v=np.zeros(3),111 q=quat.normalize(q0.copy()),112 ba=np.zeros(3),113 bp=np.zeros(3),114 P=P,115 )116117118def predict(state: EKFState, gyro: np.ndarray, accel: np.ndarray, dt: float, config: EKFConfig) -> EKFState:119 if dt <= 0:120 return state121122 R = quat.to_rotmat(state.q)123 f = accel - state.ba124 a_world = R @ f + G_WORLD125126 new_p = state.p + state.v * dt + 0.5 * a_world * dt * dt127 new_v = state.v + a_world * dt128 dq = quat.from_axis_angle(gyro * dt)129 new_q = quat.normalize(quat.multiply(state.q, dq))130 new_ba = state.ba.copy()131 new_bp = state.bp.copy()132133 F = np.eye(NDIM)134 F[IP : IP + 3, IV : IV + 3] = np.eye(3) * dt135 F[IV : IV + 3, ITH : ITH + 3] = -R @ skew(f) * dt136 F[IV : IV + 3, IBA : IBA + 3] = -R * dt137 F[ITH : ITH + 3, ITH : ITH + 3] = np.eye(3) - skew(gyro) * dt138 # IBP block: identity (near-constant bias), off-diagonals stay zero139140 Q = np.zeros((NDIM, NDIM))141 Q[IP : IP + 3, IP : IP + 3] = (config.sigma_pos_process**2 * dt) * np.eye(3)142 Q[IV : IV + 3, IV : IV + 3] = (config.sigma_accel**2 * dt) * np.eye(3)143 Q[ITH : ITH + 3, ITH : ITH + 3] = (config.sigma_gyro**2 * dt) * np.eye(3)144 Q[IBA : IBA + 3, IBA : IBA + 3] = (config.sigma_ba_rw**2 * dt) * np.eye(3)145 Q[IBP : IBP + 3, IBP : IBP + 3] = (config.sigma_bp_rw**2 * dt) * np.eye(3)146147 new_P = F @ state.P @ F.T + Q148149 return EKFState(p=new_p, v=new_v, q=new_q, ba=new_ba, bp=new_bp, P=new_P)150151152def _apply_correction(state: EKFState, residual: np.ndarray, H: np.ndarray, R_meas: np.ndarray) -> EKFState:153 S = H @ state.P @ H.T + R_meas154 K = state.P @ H.T @ np.linalg.inv(S)155 dx = K @ residual156157 I = np.eye(NDIM)158 IKH = I - K @ H159 new_P = IKH @ state.P @ IKH.T + K @ R_meas @ K.T # Joseph form, numerically robust160161 new_p = state.p + dx[IP : IP + 3]162 new_v = state.v + dx[IV : IV + 3]163 new_q = quat.normalize(quat.multiply(state.q, quat.small_angle_quat(dx[ITH : ITH + 3])))164 new_ba = state.ba + dx[IBA : IBA + 3]165 new_bp = state.bp + dx[IBP : IBP + 3]166167 return EKFState(p=new_p, v=new_v, q=new_q, ba=new_ba, bp=new_bp, P=new_P)168169170def correct_pose_source(171 state: EKFState, pos_meas: np.ndarray, quat_meas: np.ndarray, confidence: float, config: EKFConfig172) -> EKFState:173 H = np.zeros((6, NDIM))174 H[0:3, IP : IP + 3] = np.eye(3)175 H[0:3, IBP : IBP + 3] = np.eye(3) # measurement is p + bp, not p alone176 H[3:6, ITH : ITH + 3] = np.eye(3)177178 r_p = pos_meas - (state.p + state.bp)179 r_theta = quat.local_angular_error(state.q, quat_meas)180 residual = np.concatenate([r_p, r_theta])181182 c = max(confidence, config.min_confidence_floor)183 sigma_pos = config.pose_pos_sigma_base_m / c184 sigma_ori = config.pose_ori_sigma_base_rad / c185 R_meas = np.diag([sigma_pos**2] * 3 + [sigma_ori**2] * 3)186187 return _apply_correction(state, residual, H, R_meas)188189190def correct_rtk(state: EKFState, enu_meas: np.ndarray, fix: str, config: EKFConfig) -> EKFState:191 H = np.zeros((3, NDIM))192 H[0:3, IP : IP + 3] = np.eye(3) # RTK observes true p directly, no bias term193194 r = enu_meas - state.p195 sigma = config.rtk_fixed_sigma_m if fix == "rtk_fixed" else config.rtk_float_sigma_m196 R_meas = (sigma**2) * np.eye(3)197198 return _apply_correction(state, r, H, R_meas)199

1"""Drives the EKF over the merged, time-ordered IMU / pose_source / RTK2event stream. Shared by the self-check validation run and the real3pipeline. Deliberately separate from dropout/publish/transform concerns --4this module only answers "what does the fused state look like over time,"5given an already-validated (accepted) pose_source list.6"""78from dataclasses import dataclass910import numpy as np1112from orion import ekf13from orion.types import ImuSample, PoseSourceSample, RtkSample1415_PRIORITY = {"pose": 0, "rtk": 1, "imu": 2}161718@dataclass19class FusionEvent:20 t: float21 kind: str # "pose" | "rtk" | "imu"22 payload: object232425@dataclass26class TraceEntry:27 t: float28 state: ekf.EKFState29 event_kind: str30 pose_source_seq: int | None = None # set on "pose" events, for dropout tracking downstream313233def build_event_stream(34 pose_source_accepted: list, imu_samples: list, rtk_samples: list35) -> list:36 events = []37 events += [FusionEvent(s.t_source, "pose", s) for s in pose_source_accepted]38 events += [FusionEvent(s.t, "rtk", s) for s in rtk_samples]39 events += [FusionEvent(s.t, "imu", s) for s in imu_samples]40 events.sort(key=lambda e: (e.t, _PRIORITY[e.kind]))41 return events424344def run_fusion(45 pose_source_accepted: list, imu_samples: list, rtk_samples: list, config: ekf.EKFConfig46) -> list:47 """Returns a trace: list[TraceEntry], one entry per processed event,48 covering the whole log duration."""49 events = build_event_stream(pose_source_accepted, imu_samples, rtk_samples)5051 state = None52 last_state_t = None53 last_imu: ImuSample | None = None54 trace: list[TraceEntry] = []5556 for e in events:57 if state is None:58 if e.kind != "pose":59 # can't initialize from IMU/RTK alone; wait for the first pose_source fix60 continue61 s: PoseSourceSample = e.payload62 state = ekf.init_state(s.pos_m, s.quat_wxyz, config)63 last_state_t = e.t64 trace.append(TraceEntry(e.t, state, "pose", s.seq))65 continue6667 dt = e.t - last_state_t68 if dt > 0 and last_imu is not None:69 state = ekf.predict(state, last_imu.gyro_rad_s, last_imu.accel_m_s2, dt, config)70 last_state_t = e.t7172 if e.kind == "imu":73 last_imu = e.payload74 trace.append(TraceEntry(e.t, state, "imu", None))75 elif e.kind == "pose":76 s: PoseSourceSample = e.payload77 state = ekf.correct_pose_source(state, s.pos_m, s.quat_wxyz, s.confidence, config)78 trace.append(TraceEntry(e.t, state, "pose", s.seq))79 elif e.kind == "rtk":80 r: RtkSample = e.payload81 state = ekf.correct_rtk(state, r.enu_m, r.fix, config)82 trace.append(TraceEntry(e.t, state, "rtk", None))8384 return trace858687def state_at_or_before(trace: list, t: float):88 """Nearest trace entry at or before time t (linear scan is fine at this89 scale -- callers use it sparingly, e.g. 10 self-check keyframes)."""90 best = None91 for entry in trace:92 if entry.t <= t + 1e-9:93 best = entry94 else:95 break96 return best97

1"""Wires validator -> EKF fusion -> dropout gate -> target transform -> 2publisher into the actual service. Publishes on a FIXED output clock 3(independent of input jitter/rate), decoupled from how densely pose_source 4happens to sample -- this is what guarantees the >=24 Hz floor regardless of 5input irregularities. 6 7Replay/latency pacing: UNTHROTTLED (as-fast-as-possible) batch replay, not 8simulated real-time playback with artificial sleeps to match the log's 930s wall-clock duration. Disclosed explicitly because the plan requires it: 10the p50/p95 "end-to-end replay latency" reported here is genuine measured 11ingest-to-publish wall-clock latency in THIS implementation (numpy/Python 12per-event processing time), not a simulation of real 24-72h field latency. 13""" 14 15import time 16from dataclasses import dataclass 17 18from orion import ekf 19from orion.dropout import DropoutConfig, DropoutTracker 20from orion.transform import TargetTransform 21from orion.types import LatencySample, OutputRecord, PoseSourceSample, RtkSample 22from orion.validator import ValidatorConfig, validate_pose_source 23 24_PRIORITY = {"pose": 0, "rtk": 1, "imu": 2, "publish": 3} 25 26 27@dataclass 28class PipelineConfig: 29 config_version: str = "v1" 30 publish_rate_hz: float = 48.0 31 ekf_config: "ekf.EKFConfig" = None 32 validator_config: ValidatorConfig = None 33 dropout_config: DropoutConfig = None 34 35 def __post_init__(self): 36 if self.ekf_config is None: 37 self.ekf_config = ekf.EKFConfig() 38 if self.validator_config is None: 39 self.validator_config = ValidatorConfig() 40 if self.dropout_config is None: 41 self.dropout_config = DropoutConfig() 42 43 44@dataclass 45class PipelineResult: 46 outputs: list 47 rejected: list 48 latency_samples: list 49 50 51def _build_events(pose_source_accepted, imu_samples, rtk_samples, publish_rate_hz): 52 events = [] 53 events += [(s.t_source, "pose", s) for s in pose_source_accepted] 54 events += [(s.t, "rtk", s) for s in rtk_samples] 55 events += [(s.t, "imu", s) for s in imu_samples] 56 57 if pose_source_accepted: 58 t0 = pose_source_accepted[0].t_source 59 t_end = max( 60 [s.t_source for s in pose_source_accepted] 61 + [s.t for s in imu_samples] 62 + [s.t for s in rtk_samples] 63 ) 64 dt = 1.0 / publish_rate_hz 65 n_ticks = int((t_end - t0) / dt) + 1 66 events += [(t0 + i * dt, "publish", None) for i in range(n_ticks)] 67 68 events.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0], _PRIORITY[e[1]])) 69 return events 70 71 72def run_pipeline(log, config: PipelineConfig) -> PipelineResult: 73 accepted, rejected = validate_pose_source(log.pose_source, config.validator_config) 74 events = _build_events(accepted, log.imu, log.rtk, config.publish_rate_hz) 75 76 state = None 77 last_state_t = None 78 last_imu = None 79 last_pose_confidence = 1.0 80 transform = TargetTransform() 81 dropout_tracker = DropoutTracker(config.dropout_config) 82 83 outputs: list[OutputRecord] = [] 84 latency_samples: list[LatencySample] = [] 85 last_ingest_wall_s = time.perf_counter() 86 seq_out = 0 87 88 for t, kind, payload in events: 89 if state is None: 90 if kind != "pose": 91 continue 92 s: PoseSourceSample = payload 93 state = ekf.init_state(s.pos_m, s.quat_wxyz, config.ekf_config) 94 dropout_tracker.on_pose_source_accepted(s.t_source, s.t_captured) 95 last_pose_confidence = s.confidence 96 last_state_t = t 97 last_ingest_wall_s = time.perf_counter() 98 continue 99 100 dt = t - last_state_t 101 if dt > 0 and last_imu is not None: 102 state = ekf.predict(state, last_imu.gyro_rad_s, last_imu.accel_m_s2, dt, config.ekf_config) 103 last_state_t = t 104 105 if kind == "imu": 106 last_imu = payload 107 last_ingest_wall_s = time.perf_counter() 108 elif kind == "pose": 109 s: PoseSourceSample = payload 110 state = ekf.correct_pose_source(state, s.pos_m, s.quat_wxyz, s.confidence, config.ekf_config) 111 dropout_tracker.on_pose_source_accepted(s.t_source, s.t_captured) 112 last_pose_confidence = s.confidence 113 last_ingest_wall_s = time.perf_counter() 114 elif kind == "rtk": 115 r: RtkSample = payload 116 state = ekf.correct_rtk(state, r.enu_m, r.fix, config.ekf_config) 117 last_ingest_wall_s = time.perf_counter() 118 elif kind == "publish": 119 if not transform.has_origin: 120 # origin = the pipeline's own fused position estimate at the 121 # first published sample (may already reflect a same-instant 122 # RTK correction) -- not the raw pose_source reading. 123 transform.set_origin_from_first_sample(state.p) 124 pos_target, quat_target = transform.apply(state.p, state.q) 125 pos_out, quat_out, conf_out, pub_state, source_age_s = dropout_tracker.publish_state( 126 t, pos_target, quat_target, last_pose_confidence 127 ) 128 record = OutputRecord( 129 seq=seq_out, 130 t_source=t, 131 pos_target=pos_out, 132 quat_target=quat_out, 133 confidence=conf_out, 134 source_age_s=source_age_s, 135 state=pub_state, 136 ) 137 outputs.append(record) 138 publish_wall_s = time.perf_counter() 139 latency_samples.append( 140 LatencySample( 141 seq=seq_out, 142 ingest_wall_s=last_ingest_wall_s, 143 publish_wall_s=publish_wall_s, 144 latency_s=publish_wall_s - last_ingest_wall_s, 145 ) 146 ) 147 seq_out += 1 148 149 return PipelineResult(outputs=outputs, rejected=rejected, latency_samples=latency_samples) 150

1"""Quaternion helpers. Convention throughout: q = [w, x, y, z], body->world2(v_world = R(q) @ v_body), matching the source log's stated convention."""34import numpy as np567def normalize(q: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:8 n = np.linalg.norm(q)9 if n < 1e-12:10 return np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])11 return q / n121314def multiply(q1: np.ndarray, q2: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:15 """Hamilton product q1 * q2 (apply q2 first, then q1's rotation, i.e.16 R(q1*q2) = R(q1) @ R(q2))."""17 w1, x1, y1, z1 = q118 w2, x2, y2, z2 = q219 return np.array([20 w1 * w2 - x1 * x2 - y1 * y2 - z1 * z2,21 w1 * x2 + x1 * w2 + y1 * z2 - z1 * y2,22 w1 * y2 - x1 * z2 + y1 * w2 + z1 * x2,23 w1 * z2 + x1 * y2 - y1 * x2 + z1 * w2,24 ])252627def conjugate(q: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:28 return np.array([q[0], -q[1], -q[2], -q[3]])293031def to_rotmat(q: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:32 w, x, y, z = normalize(q)33 return np.array([34 [1 - 2 * (y * y + z * z), 2 * (x * y - z * w), 2 * (x * z + y * w)],35 [2 * (x * y + z * w), 1 - 2 * (x * x + z * z), 2 * (y * z - x * w)],36 [2 * (x * z - y * w), 2 * (y * z + x * w), 1 - 2 * (x * x + y * y)],37 ])383940def rotmat_to_quat(R: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:41 """Shepperd's method - numerically robust for any proper rotation matrix."""42 m00, m01, m02 = R[0]43 m10, m11, m12 = R[1]44 m20, m21, m22 = R[2]45 trace = m00 + m11 + m2246 if trace > 0:47 s = 0.5 / np.sqrt(trace + 1.0)48 w = 0.25 / s49 x = (m21 - m12) * s50 y = (m02 - m20) * s51 z = (m10 - m01) * s52 elif m00 > m11 and m00 > m22:53 s = 2.0 * np.sqrt(1.0 + m00 - m11 - m22)54 w = (m21 - m12) / s55 x = 0.25 * s56 y = (m01 + m10) / s57 z = (m02 + m20) / s58 elif m11 > m22:59 s = 2.0 * np.sqrt(1.0 + m11 - m00 - m22)60 w = (m02 - m20) / s61 x = (m01 + m10) / s62 y = 0.25 * s63 z = (m12 + m21) / s64 else:65 s = 2.0 * np.sqrt(1.0 + m22 - m00 - m11)66 w = (m10 - m01) / s67 x = (m02 + m20) / s68 y = (m12 + m21) / s69 z = 0.25 * s70 return normalize(np.array([w, x, y, z]))717273def rotate_vector(q: np.ndarray, v: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:74 return to_rotmat(q) @ v757677def from_axis_angle(axis_angle: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:78 """Exact exponential map: axis_angle = axis * angle (rad)."""79 angle = np.linalg.norm(axis_angle)80 if angle < 1e-12:81 return np.array([1.0, *(0.5 * axis_angle)])82 axis = axis_angle / angle83 half = 0.5 * angle84 return np.array([np.cos(half), *(axis * np.sin(half))])858687def small_angle_quat(delta_theta: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:88 """First-order approximation used to inject a small error-state rotation89 back into the nominal quaternion (standard error-state EKF convention)."""90 return normalize(np.array([1.0, *(0.5 * delta_theta)]))919293def local_angular_error(q_pred: np.ndarray, q_meas: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:94 """Small-angle rotation vector delta_theta, expressed in the BODY frame,95 such that q_meas ~= q_pred (x) exp(delta_theta / 2). This matches the96 right-multiplicative (local/body-frame) error-state convention used by97 the EKF's process model (q_new = q (x) delta_q from gyro integration),98 so the measurement Jacobian for this residual is simply H_theta = I.99 Sign-corrected for the shortest-path rotation."""100 dq = multiply(conjugate(q_pred), q_meas)101 if dq[0] < 0:102 dq = -dq103 return 2.0 * dq[1:]104

1"""Target-frame transform: source (ENU right-handed meters, quat wxyz2body->world) -> target (X=East,Y=Up,Z=North left-handed, centimeters,3quat xyzw), origin translated to the first published sample.45No literal matrix is given by the contract; this is composed from the6stated conventions. See the plan's "Target transform derivation" section7for the reasoning.8"""910import numpy as np1112from orion import quat as q1314METERS_TO_CM = 100.01516# Source basis order is (East, North, Up). Target basis order is17# (East, Up, North) -- i.e. swap the North and Up components. As a matrix18# acting on a column vector [E,N,U]^T -> [E,U,N]^T:19# target_x = source_x (East)20# target_y = source_z (Up)21# target_z = source_y (North)22# This is a permutation with one transposition (odd), so det(P) = -1,23# correctly flipping handedness right -> left.24_P = np.array(25 [26 [1.0, 0.0, 0.0],27 [0.0, 0.0, 1.0],28 [0.0, 1.0, 0.0],29 ]30)313233def axis_permutation_matrix() -> np.ndarray:34 return _P.copy()353637def permute_position(pos_enu_m: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:38 """ENU meters -> (East,Up,North) meters, no scale/origin applied yet."""39 return _P @ pos_enu_m404142def permute_orientation(quat_wxyz_body_to_world: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:43 """Re-express a body->world rotation in the permuted (East,Up,North)44 world basis via a similarity transform R' = P R P^T (P is its own45 inverse: it's an orthogonal involution). This is the correct way to46 carry a rotation across a change of basis -- NOT a component relabel."""47 R = q.to_rotmat(quat_wxyz_body_to_world)48 R_prime = _P @ R @ _P.T49 return q.rotmat_to_quat(R_prime)505152class TargetTransform:53 """Stateful only in that it remembers the origin (target-frame,54 centimeters, permuted+scaled) established from the first published55 sample. Everything else is a pure function of its inputs."""5657 def __init__(self) -> None:58 self._origin_cm: np.ndarray | None = None5960 @property61 def has_origin(self) -> bool:62 return self._origin_cm is not None6364 def set_origin_from_first_sample(self, pos_enu_m: np.ndarray) -> None:65 self._origin_cm = permute_position(pos_enu_m) * METERS_TO_CM6667 def apply(self, pos_enu_m: np.ndarray, quat_wxyz_body_to_world: np.ndarray):68 """Returns (pos_target_cm, quat_target_xyzw)."""69 if self._origin_cm is None:70 raise RuntimeError("origin not set; call set_origin_from_first_sample first")7172 pos_cm = permute_position(pos_enu_m) * METERS_TO_CM - self._origin_cm73 quat_wxyz_target = permute_orientation(quat_wxyz_body_to_world)74 # reorder [w,x,y,z] -> [x,y,z,w]75 quat_xyzw_target = np.array(76 [quat_wxyz_target[1], quat_wxyz_target[2], quat_wxyz_target[3], quat_wxyz_target[0]]77 )78 return pos_cm, quat_xyzw_target79

1"""Data model for input streams, self-check, and output records.23Quaternions are numpy arrays [w, x, y, z] (source convention) internally;4only the final output record stores the target [x, y, z, w] order the5contract requires.6"""78from dataclasses import dataclass, field910import numpy as np111213@dataclass14class PoseSourceSample:15 seq: int16 t_source: float17 t_captured: float18 pos_m: np.ndarray # ENU meters, shape (3,)19 quat_wxyz: np.ndarray # shape (4,)20 confidence: float21 state: str222324@dataclass25class ImuSample:26 t: float27 gyro_rad_s: np.ndarray28 accel_m_s2: np.ndarray293031@dataclass32class RtkSample:33 t: float34 enu_m: np.ndarray35 fix: str363738@dataclass39class SensorLog:40 fixture: str41 duration_s: float42 pose_source: list = field(default_factory=list)43 imu: list = field(default_factory=list)44 rtk: list = field(default_factory=list)454647@dataclass48class SelfCheckKeyframe:49 t: float50 pos_m: np.ndarray51 quat_wxyz: np.ndarray525354@dataclass55class SelfCheckBands:56 position_median_m: float57 position_p95_m: float58 orientation_median_deg: float59 orientation_p95_deg: float60 publish_rate_hz_min: float616263@dataclass64class SelfCheck:65 keyframes: list66 bands: SelfCheckBands676869@dataclass70class RejectedObservation:71 seq: int72 t_source: float73 reason: str747576@dataclass77class OutputRecord:78 seq: int79 t_source: float80 pos_target: np.ndarray # cm, shape (3,)81 quat_target: np.ndarray # [x, y, z, w]82 confidence: float83 source_age_s: float84 state: str # tracking | degraded | lost858687@dataclass88class LatencySample:89 seq: int90 ingest_wall_s: float91 publish_wall_s: float92 latency_s: float93
pythonorion-pose-py/orion/unreal_frame.py
1"""Bonus only: target frame (X=East, Y=Up, Z=North, left-handed, cm,2quat [x,y,z,w]) -> Unreal's native world frame (X=Forward, Y=Right, Z=Up,3left-handed, cm, FQuat stored as (X,Y,Z,W)).45Units and quaternion storage order already match the contract's target6frame, so this is ONLY an axis permutation -- same technique as7transform.py, just a different remap. "Forward"/"Right" have no inherent8meaning in an empty Unreal level, so North->Forward, East->Right is an9arbitrary but consistent choice; swap it if your level has a different10idea of forward.1112Unlike the East<->Up swap in transform.py (a single transposition, det=-1,13which is what flips right-handed source into left-handed target), this14remap is a 3-cycle (E,U,N) -> (N,E,U), an EVEN permutation, det=+1 --15expected, since both the contract's target frame and Unreal's world frame16are already left-handed. No handedness flip should occur here, which is17itself a check worth keeping an eye on (see test_unreal_frame.py).18"""1920import numpy as np2122from orion import quat as q2324# rows: UE_X (Forward) <- target Z (North)25# UE_Y (Right) <- target X (East)26# UE_Z (Up) <- target Y (Up)27_P2 = np.array(28 [29 [0.0, 0.0, 1.0],30 [1.0, 0.0, 0.0],31 [0.0, 1.0, 0.0],32 ]33)343536def axis_permutation_matrix() -> np.ndarray:37 return _P2.copy()383940def permute_position(pos_target_cm: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:41 return _P2 @ pos_target_cm424344def permute_orientation_xyzw(quat_target_xyzw: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:45 """Takes and returns [x,y,z,w] (the storage order both the contract's46 target frame and Unreal's FQuat use) -- converts to [w,x,y,z]47 internally for quat.py's math, then back."""48 x, y, z, w = quat_target_xyzw49 q_wxyz = np.array([w, x, y, z])50 R = q.to_rotmat(q_wxyz)51 R_prime = _P2 @ R @ _P2.T52 w2, x2, y2, z2 = q.rotmat_to_quat(R_prime)53 return np.array([x2, y2, z2, w2])545556def to_unreal(pos_target_cm: np.ndarray, quat_target_xyzw: np.ndarray):57 """Returns (pos_ue_cm, quat_ue_xyzw). No origin offset applied here --58 the caller decides where the stream's own origin (0,0,0 in target59 frame, per Part 1) should sit in the level, e.g. by placing an anchor60 actor or just using world origin."""61 return permute_position(pos_target_cm), permute_orientation_xyzw(quat_target_xyzw)62
pythonorion-pose-py/orion/validator.py
1"""Validates the pose_source stream in ingestion (array) order, rejecting2duplicate / stale / out-of-order packets with a disclosed reason. Checks run3in a specific, deliberate order so each fault is classified by its most4specific cause rather than falling through to a generic catch-all:56 1. t_captured after t_source (physically impossible) or an implausible7 source-to-capture lag -> "capture_after_source_time" / "implausible_capture_lag"8 2. exact duplicate of the last accepted sample -> "duplicate"9 3. seq not strictly greater than the last accepted seq -> "non_monotonic_seq"10 4. t_source not strictly greater than the last accepted t_source -> "out_of_order_t_source"1112This ordering was derived from three concrete faults found in the dev log13(see the plan): an exact duplicate packet, a reused seq number pointing to a14later time, and an out-of-order injected record with a future t_captured.15"""1617from dataclasses import dataclass1819import numpy as np2021from orion.types import PoseSourceSample, RejectedObservation222324@dataclass25class ValidatorConfig:26 max_capture_lag_s: float = 1.0 # max plausible (t_source - t_captured)272829def validate_pose_source(30 samples: list, config: ValidatorConfig | None = None31) -> tuple[list, list]:32 if config is None:33 config = ValidatorConfig()3435 accepted: list[PoseSourceSample] = []36 rejected: list[RejectedObservation] = []3738 last_seq = None39 last_t_source = None40 last_t_captured = None41 last_pos = None4243 for s in samples:44 lag = s.t_source - s.t_captured4546 if lag < 0:47 rejected.append(RejectedObservation(s.seq, s.t_source, "capture_after_source_time"))48 continue49 if lag > config.max_capture_lag_s:50 rejected.append(RejectedObservation(s.seq, s.t_source, "implausible_capture_lag"))51 continue5253 if (54 last_seq is not None55 and s.seq == last_seq56 and s.t_source == last_t_source57 and s.t_captured == last_t_captured58 and np.array_equal(s.pos_m, last_pos)59 ):60 rejected.append(RejectedObservation(s.seq, s.t_source, "duplicate"))61 continue6263 if last_seq is not None and s.seq <= last_seq:64 rejected.append(RejectedObservation(s.seq, s.t_source, "non_monotonic_seq"))65 continue6667 if last_t_source is not None and s.t_source <= last_t_source:68 rejected.append(RejectedObservation(s.seq, s.t_source, "out_of_order_t_source"))69 continue7071 accepted.append(s)72 last_seq = s.seq73 last_t_source = s.t_source74 last_t_captured = s.t_captured75 last_pos = s.pos_m7677 return accepted, rejected78

1# Part 1 - Measured Report23Config used for both runs: `config/config_v1.json` (`config_version: v1`), unmodified between the4dev run and the eval run. Full reasoning behind every parameter is documented in5`orion/ekf.py` (`EKFConfig`) and `orion/dropout.py`.67## 1. Pose rate held89Both runs publish on a fixed 48 Hz output clock (contract floor: 24 Hz), decoupled from input10jitter.1112| Run | records | duration | dt (constant) | rate |13|------|---------|----------|--------------------|----------|14| dev | 1440 | 30.0 s | 0.0208333 s | 48.00 Hz |15| eval | 1440 | 30.0 s | 0.0208333 s | 48.00 Hz |1617`dt` has zero jitter (min == max in both runs) because publish ticks are generated on their own18fixed schedule, independent of when sensor samples happen to arrive.1920## 2. Source-age behavior across the drop-outs2122Both logs contain the same two dropout spans (same fixture generation pattern): the tracker's23state transitions land at identical timestamps in both runs.2425| event | t_source | source_age_s |26|--------------------------------|-----------|---------------|27| tracking (normal) | 1000.000 | ~0.012 |28| -> degraded (span 1) | 1011.354 | 0.3745 |29| -> lost (span 1) | 1011.896 | 0.9162 |30| -> tracking (span 1 ends) | 1013.000 | 0.012 |31| -> degraded (span 2) | 1021.854 | 0.3745 |32| -> lost (span 2) | 1022.396 | 0.9162 |33| -> tracking (span 2 ends) | 1022.500 | 0.012 |3435`source_age_s` grows monotonically through every hold and resets on resync, in both runs.36Position and orientation are frozen at the last known-good value for the full duration of each37hold (verified in `tests/test_dropout.py` and by direct inspection of both output files: no38sample-to-sample change in `pos_target`/`quat_target` while `state != tracking`). State counts:391330 tracking / 52 degraded / 58 lost, identical in both runs.4041Thresholds (0.35 s degraded / 0.9 s lost) were set conservatively below the ~1.0 s shortest real42dropout so genuine faults always trip the state machine while ordinary single-sample rejections43(a few ms apart) never do - confirmed by dropout timestamps landing well after each span's actual44start and returning to `tracking` at exactly the moment `pose_source` data resumes.4546## 3. Coordinate-conversion correctness4748The contract gives conventions, not a literal matrix (source: ENU right-handed meters, quat49`[w,x,y,z]`; target: left-handed centimeters, X=East/Y=Up/Z=North, quat `[x,y,z,w]`, origin at the50first published sample). Verified two ways:5152- **Unit tests** (`tests/test_transform.py`, 7/7 passing): axis-permutation determinant flips sign53 (handedness check), a known ENU vector maps to the expected East/Up/North order, m->cm scaling,54 quaternion reorder. The highest-priority test checks the defining correctness property of a55 *point transform* under a change of basis directly: `permute(R @ v) == R'(permute(v))` for56 random rotations/vectors, plus a hand-computed concrete 90 degree case - this is what would catch57 a silent quaternion-component-relabeling bug that a determinant or round-trip check would miss.58- **Runtime confirmation**: first published sample in both runs is exactly `[0.0, 0.0, 0.0]` cm59 (origin correctly anchored), and the self-check gate (below) validates the pre-transform fusion60 independently confirms handedness/scale/quaternion-order sanity per the challenge's stated61 purpose for the self-check.6263## 4. Self-check gate (dev log only - this is the only ground truth available)6465`tests/test_selfcheck.py`, run on the pre-transform fused pose against `orion-dev-selfcheck.json`'s6610 keyframes:6768| metric | measured | band | result |69|------------------------|---------|-------|--------|70| position median (m) | 0.0267 | 0.03 | PASS |71| position p95 (m) | 0.0682 | 0.08 | PASS |72| orientation median (deg) | 0.0067 | 0.8 | PASS |73| orientation p95 (deg) | 0.3779 | 2.5 | PASS |7475The worst single point (0.090 m position / 0.68 deg orientation) falls exactly at t=1012.0, inside76dropout span 1 (1010.99-1013.00) where `pose_source` has no data at all - the EKF is running on77IMU+RTK alone there, so this is the expected accuracy floor for that specific gap, not a general78fusion error. All other 9 points are well inside both bands.7980No self-check exists for the eval log by design (held-out truth). Confidence that the eval run is81correct rests on: the pipeline and config are byte-for-byte identical between the two runs, the82eval log's fault/dropout pattern matches the dev log's exactly (confirming it's the same fixture83generation, not a different scenario), and the self-check gate above already passed *before* the84eval log was touched.8586## 5. End-to-end replay latency (p50 / p95)8788**Pacing disclosure**: replay is unthrottled (as-fast-as-possible) batch processing, not simulated89real-time playback with artificial pacing to match the log's 30 s nominal duration. The measured90latency is genuine ingest-to-publish wall-clock time in this implementation (Python/numpy91processing time per event), not a simulation of real 24-72h field latency. This tradeoff is92disclosed rather than spending real wall-clock time sleeping to imitate 30 s of live playback.9394| Run | p50 | p95 | max |95|------|-----------|-----------|-----------|96| dev | 0.080 ms | 0.090 ms | 0.478 ms |97| eval | 0.074 ms | 0.083 ms | 0.329 ms |9899## 6. Rejected observations100101Both logs reject exactly 3 `pose_source` packets, with identical seq numbers and reasons (same102fixture-seeded faults in both):103104| seq | t_source | reason |105|------|-------------|-----------------------------|106| 200 | 1001.666667 | duplicate |107| 3240 | 1002.0 | capture_after_source_time |108| 500 | 1007.5 | non_monotonic_seq |109110Full lists: `deliverables/rejected-observations.jsonl` (eval), `out_dev/rejected.jsonl` (dev).111112## 7. Disclosures (stated explicitly, not buried)113114- **No timecode stream exists** in either log, despite the PDF's introductory text mentioning one.115 The contract's own `output_stream_fields` also has no timecode field. Nothing was decoded because116 there is nothing to decode - this is a discrepancy between the intro prose and the actual fixture117 contract, not an omission on our part.118- **The hard-reset resync policy causes a visible one-sample discontinuity** at the end of every119 hold (t=1013.000 and t=1022.500 in both runs): the published pose jumps directly from the held120 value to the EKF's current fused estimate, with no interpolation. This is deliberate - smoothing121 it away would risk quietly presenting part of an actual dropout as continuously tracked when it122 wasn't.123- **Origin** is the pipeline's own fused position estimate at the first published sample124 (t_source=1000.0), which already reflects a same-instant RTK correction - not the raw125 `pose_source` reading, and not the self-check keyframe's ground-truth value (the eval log has no126 self-check to anchor to, so the origin has to come from the pipeline's own output to stay127 consistent across both runs).128- **Fusion fidelity actually shipped**: the full 15-dim error-state EKF (position, velocity,129 orientation, accelerometer bias, and a `pose_source` position-bias state) - no fallback to a130 simpler filter was needed. The bias state was *not* part of the original plan; it was added131 mid-build after an initial 12-dim version passed orientation but failed the self-check on132 position (see `orion/ekf.py`'s module docstring for the full diagnosis: raw `pose_source`133 orientation matches self-check truth to floating-point precision everywhere outside the dropout,134 while its position error grows over the run and RTK's doesn't - a single scalar measurement-noise135 weight can't represent "trust this sensor locally but not for absolute position," so it became an136 explicit state instead).137- **Noise parameter selection**: most values come directly from documented/observed sensor138 characteristics (pose_source orientation trusted tightly since it doesn't drift; RTK fixed trusted139 more than float). The IMU process-noise inflation term (`sigma_accel`) was set by checking a small140 number of order-of-magnitude values against the self-check bands, which is what the self-check is141 stated to be for - not an automated fit, and it was fixed before the eval log was ever run.142143## 8. Known limitations and assumptions144145- **The accelerometer bias state (`ba`) was not observable on this trajectory.** Its filter146 uncertainty (`trace(P_ba)`) does not shrink from its initial value over either run (0.0003 ->147 0.000387 on both dev and eval) - the state stays near zero because nothing pulls it away, not148 because it's being confidently estimated. Contrast with the `pose_source` position-bias state149 `bp`, whose uncertainty collapses 0.12 -> 0.0002. `ba` is currently harmless (it never grows150 large) but it isn't earning its place in the state vector on this data.151- **Only `pose_source` packets are validated.** `imu` and `rtk` are trusted unconditionally with no152 rejection path - the contract's "reject invalid observations" rule was implemented for153 `pose_source` only, where the actual injected faults were found. Both streams were independently154 checked for duplicates/non-monotonic timestamps/non-finite values in both logs and came back clean,155 so this doesn't affect the current submission, but the code has no structural defense if either156 stream carried a fault.157- **East/North axis order is taken from the contract's "ENU" naming, not an explicit mapping.** The158 contract spells out the target axes literally (`"X=East, Y=Up, Z=North"`) but never does the same159 for the source - only the acronym "ENU" is given. Up is independently confirmed (gravity dominates160 the 3rd `accel_m_s2` component at rest), but East vs. North (indices 0 vs. 1) rests entirely on the161 acronym. The self-check cannot catch a swap here: it compares fused position/orientation against162 truth in raw array order, pre-transform, so it's blind to any error introduced by `transform.py`'s163 axis assignment specifically.164- **`source_age_s`'s "now" is the replay timeline (`t_source`), not wall-clock time.** The contract165 defines it only as `"now - t_captured"`. Wall-clock time would be meaningless for a batch replay166 (it would just measure processing speed); the output's own advancing `t_source` is the only167 reading that keeps `source_age_s` meaningful during a hold, but it's an interpretive choice, not168 a literal restatement of the contract.169- **Confidence is held constant during a pose hold**, not decayed. The rule allows the held pose170 itself to use "a disclosed decay" instead of a flat hold; this implementation reads that as171 applying to position/orientation and freezes confidence alongside them rather than decaying it172 toward zero as `source_age_s` grows. A stricter reading could expect confidence itself to decay.173174## 9. Bonus - Unreal Engine live verification (optional)175176Not required to pass, done because Unreal was available. The eval output (`unreal_bridge/orion-eval-output.csv`,177a direct export of `deliverables/orion-eval-output.jsonl`) was fed into a `CineCameraActor` in Unreal178Engine 5.6 via a small C++ actor (`unreal_bridge/OrionCameraDriver.h/.cpp`) that applies one further179axis remap - the contract's target frame (X=East, Y=Up, Z=North) into Unreal's native frame180(X=Forward, Y=Right, Z=Up) - and logs a render-space readback (both to the log and on-screen) of the181actor's actual transform after each set, so the check is against what Unreal itself holds, not just182what was requested.183184Run live in the editor, this passed cleanly, with the log itself as evidence:185186- **Origin**: `seq=0` gives `intended=(0,0,0)` and `readback_loc=(0,0,0)` - matches Part 1's origin187 definition (first published sample = zero) after the extra Unreal-frame conversion too.188- **Round-trip fidelity**: `readback_loc` matched `intended` exactly on every logged line across the189 full 1440-record run - `SetActorLocationAndRotation` introduced no discrepancy between the intended190 and actual Unreal transform.191- **Dropout hold and resync, confirmed inside the engine**: at `seq=552/576/600` (`degraded`/`lost`/192 `lost`) the logged position is identical across all three - `(-26.6,-32.6,-62.2)` - then jumps to a193 new value the instant `seq=624` returns to `tracking`. Converting those sequence numbers back to194 source time (`t = 1000 + seq/48`) lands at `t≈1011.5→1013.0`, matching dropout span 1 as measured195 independently in section 2 of this report. This is the same dropout-hold-then-hard-cut-resync196 behavior verified three separate times now: in the Python EKF/dropout unit tests, in the coordinate197 math's own unit tests (`tests/test_unreal_frame.py`), and now rendering live inside Unreal.198199One honesty note: the C++ side of this (the actual Unreal API calls, as opposed to the coordinate200math, which was unit-tested beforehand) was written without a live Unreal project available to test201against, and is confirmed working here only because it was run for real afterward - it was not a sure202thing going in.203

1"""The go/no-go gate: fused (pre-target-transform) pose at the self-check's210 sparse keyframe timestamps must fall inside its tolerance bands. This is3the only accuracy ground truth available before submission."""45import numpy as np67from orion import ekf, quat8from orion.fusion import run_fusion, state_at_or_before9from orion.json_io import load_self_check, load_sensor_log10from orion.validator import validate_pose_source111213def test_fused_pose_within_selfcheck_bands():14 log = load_sensor_log("../orion-dev-log.json")15 self_check = load_self_check("../orion-dev-selfcheck.json")1617 accepted, _rejected = validate_pose_source(log.pose_source)18 config = ekf.EKFConfig()19 trace = run_fusion(accepted, log.imu, log.rtk, config)2021 pos_errors_m = []22 ori_errors_deg = []23 for kf in self_check.keyframes:24 entry = state_at_or_before(trace, kf.t)25 assert entry is not None, f"no trace entry at/before t={kf.t}"26 assert abs(entry.t - kf.t) < 0.02, f"nearest trace entry too far from keyframe t={kf.t}"2728 pos_err = np.linalg.norm(entry.state.p - kf.pos_m)29 pos_errors_m.append(pos_err)3031 ang_err_rad = np.linalg.norm(quat.local_angular_error(entry.state.q, kf.quat_wxyz))32 ori_errors_deg.append(np.degrees(ang_err_rad))3334 pos_errors_m = np.array(pos_errors_m)35 ori_errors_deg = np.array(ori_errors_deg)3637 print(f"\nposition errors (m): {np.round(pos_errors_m, 4)}")38 print(f"orientation errors (deg): {np.round(ori_errors_deg, 4)}")39 print(f"position median={np.median(pos_errors_m):.4f} p95={np.percentile(pos_errors_m, 95):.4f}")40 print(f"orientation median={np.median(ori_errors_deg):.4f} p95={np.percentile(ori_errors_deg, 95):.4f}")4142 assert np.median(pos_errors_m) <= self_check.bands.position_median_m43 assert np.percentile(pos_errors_m, 95) <= self_check.bands.position_p95_m44 assert np.median(ori_errors_deg) <= self_check.bands.orientation_median_deg45 assert np.percentile(ori_errors_deg, 95) <= self_check.bands.orientation_p95_deg46

1import numpy as np23from orion import quat as q4from orion import transform567def test_axis_permutation_determinant_flips_handedness():8 P = transform.axis_permutation_matrix()9 assert np.isclose(np.linalg.det(P), -1.0)10 # and it's an involution (its own inverse) since it's a single swap11 assert np.allclose(P @ P, np.eye(3))121314def test_position_permutation_maps_enu_to_e_up_north():15 # source ENU: East=1, North=2, Up=316 pos_enu = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])17 pos_target_order = transform.permute_position(pos_enu)18 # target order is (East, Up, North) -> (1, 3, 2)19 assert np.allclose(pos_target_order, np.array([1.0, 3.0, 2.0]))202122def test_quaternion_change_of_basis_is_self_consistent_for_point_transform():23 """The contract specifies a 'point transform'. 90 degrees about the source Up axis (Z): body x-axis (East) -> North.51 q_src = q.from_axis_angle(np.array([0.0, 0.0, np.pi / 2]))52 east = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0])53 rotated_src = q.rotate_vector(q_src, east)54 assert np.allclose(rotated_src, np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), atol=1e-9) # -> North5556 q_tgt = transform.permute_orientation(q_src)57 east_tgt = transform.permute_position(east) # East axis unchanged: (1,0,0)58 rotated_tgt = q.rotate_vector(q_tgt, east_tgt)59 expected_tgt = transform.permute_position(rotated_src) # North -> target Z: (0,0,1)60 assert np.allclose(rotated_tgt, expected_tgt, atol=1e-9)61 assert np.allclose(expected_tgt, np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), atol=1e-9)626364def test_apply_sets_origin_to_zero_for_first_sample():65 t = transform.TargetTransform()66 pos0 = np.array([0.018569, 1.054026, 1.533675])67 quat0 = np.array([0.9968075, 0.06209953, 0.05008713, -0.00312035])68 t.set_origin_from_first_sample(pos0)69 pos_cm, quat_xyzw = t.apply(pos0, quat0)70 assert np.allclose(pos_cm, np.zeros(3), atol=1e-9)71 assert np.isclose(np.linalg.norm(quat_xyzw), 1.0)727374def test_apply_scales_meters_to_centimeters():75 t = transform.TargetTransform()76 origin = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0])77 t.set_origin_from_first_sample(origin)78 quat_identity = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])79 # 1m East, 0, 0 -> should be 100cm on target X (East)80 pos_cm, _ = t.apply(np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0]), quat_identity)81 assert np.allclose(pos_cm, np.array([100.0, 0.0, 0.0]))828384def test_quat_reorder_wxyz_to_xyzw():85 t = transform.TargetTransform()86 origin = np.zeros(3)87 t.set_origin_from_first_sample(origin)88 quat_identity_wxyz = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])89 _, quat_xyzw = t.apply(origin, quat_identity_wxyz)90 assert np.allclose(quat_xyzw, np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]))91

1"""2BONUS (optional, not required to pass): drives a CineCameraActor in the3current Unreal level from the Part 1 pose stream, and logs a render-space4readback every so often so you can see Unreal's own actor transform after5each set -- proving the round trip actually landed the camera where the6pose stream intended, not just that a value was assigned.78HONESTY NOTE: I (the AI assistant) wrote this against Unreal's documented9Python API but have no Unreal Editor available to run it against. The10coordinate math (orion/unreal_frame.py) IS tested and verified -- see11tests/test_unreal_frame.py, all passing, including a check that this12script's simplified quaternion shortcut (cycle x,y,z, keep w) is13numerically identical to the full change-of-basis derivation. The Unreal14API CALLS below (unreal.CineCameraActor, register_slate_post_tick_callback,15etc.) are standard/documented for UE5, but untested end-to-end. Treat this16as a strong first draft -- see "Troubleshooting" at the bottom.1718HOW TO RUN (Unreal 5.8):191. Edit > Plugins -> enable "Python Editor Script Plugin" if not already on20 (requires an editor restart the first time).212. Open any level (an empty default level is fine).223. Window > Output Log -- this is where readback lines print.234. Window > Developer Tools > Python (or use Output Log's own command bar24 with a "py " prefix) to get a Python input.255. Run:26 exec(open(r"D:/ML/FirstEpicChallenge/orion-pose-py/unreal_bridge/drive_camera.py").read())276. Make sure the viewport is in "Realtime" mode (clock icon, top-left of28 the viewport toolbar) so you actually see the camera move.297. It stops automatically at the end of the stream, or call stop_driving()30 in the Python console to stop early / re-run start_driving() again.31"""3233import json3435import unreal3637# ---- config ---------------------------------------------------------------38JSONL_PATH = r"D:/ML/FirstEpicChallenge/orion-pose-py/deliverables/orion-eval-output.jsonl"39PLAYBACK_SPEED = 1.0 # 1.0 = real time, matched to the stream's own t_source deltas40PRINT_EVERY_N_RECORDS = 24 # readback log cadence (~every 0.5s at the stream's 48Hz)4142# ---- target-frame (contract) -> Unreal-frame axis remap -------------------43# Target: x=East, y=Up, z=North (left-handed, cm, quat xyzw).44# Unreal: X=Forward, Y=Right, Z=Up (left-handed, cm, FQuat xyzw).45# This duplicates orion/unreal_frame.py in plain Python so the script has no46# dependency on the orion package being importable from inside Unreal's47# embedded interpreter. The full derivation lives there and is unit-tested;48# this is the numerically-verified shortcut for this specific permutation49# (a pure axis 3-cycle, no reflection -- see the module docstring there for50# why the quaternion vector part can be permuted the same simple way as the51# position, confirmed to match the full R'=P R P^T derivation to 1e-16).525354def _permute_position(pos_target_cm):55 x, y, z = pos_target_cm # target: x=East, y=Up, z=North56 return z, x, y # UE: Forward<-North, Right<-East, Up<-Up575859def _permute_orientation_xyzw(quat_target_xyzw):60 x, y, z, w = quat_target_xyzw61 return z, x, y, w626364# ---- load the stream --------------------------------------------------------65def _load_records(path):66 records = []67 with open(path, "r") as f:68 for line in f:69 line = line.strip()70 if line:71 records.append(json.loads(line))72 return records737475# ---- driving state -------------------------------------------------------------76_state = {77 "records": None,78 "index": 0,79 "elapsed": 0.0,80 "t0": None,81 "camera": None,82 "tick_handle": None,83}848586def _get_or_spawn_camera():87 actor_subsystem = unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.EditorActorSubsystem)88 for actor in actor_subsystem.get_all_level_actors():89 if isinstance(actor, unreal.CineCameraActor):90 unreal.log(f"[orion] using existing CineCameraActor: {actor.get_name()}")91 return actor92 camera = actor_subsystem.spawn_actor_from_class(93 unreal.CineCameraActor, unreal.Vector(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), unreal.Rotator(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)94 )95 unreal.log(f"[orion] spawned new CineCameraActor: {camera.get_name()}")96 return camera979899def _on_tick(delta_seconds):100 st = _state101 if st["records"] is None or st["index"] >= len(st["records"]):102 stop_driving()103 return104105 st["elapsed"] += delta_seconds * PLAYBACK_SPEED106 if st["t0"] is None:107 st["t0"] = st["records"][0]["t_source"]108109 while (110 st["index"] < len(st["records"])111 and (st["records"][st["index"]]["t_source"] - st["t0"]) <= st["elapsed"]112 ):113 rec = st["records"][st["index"]]114 pos_ue = _permute_position(rec["pos_target"])115 quat_ue = _permute_orientation_xyzw(rec["quat_target"])116117 location = unreal.Vector(*pos_ue)118 quat = unreal.Quat(x=quat_ue[0], y=quat_ue[1], z=quat_ue[2], w=quat_ue[3])119 rotator = quat.rotator()120121 st["camera"].set_actor_location_and_rotation(location, rotator, False, False)122123 if st["index"] % PRINT_EVERY_N_RECORDS == 0:124 rb_loc = st["camera"].get_actor_location()125 rb_rot = st["camera"].get_actor_rotation()126 unreal.log(127 f"[orion] seq={rec['seq']} state={rec['state']} "128 f"intended_loc=({pos_ue[0]:.1f},{pos_ue[1]:.1f},{pos_ue[2]:.1f}) "129 f"readback_loc=({rb_loc.x:.1f},{rb_loc.y:.1f},{rb_loc.z:.1f}) "130 f"readback_rot=({rb_rot.roll:.2f},{rb_rot.pitch:.2f},{rb_rot.yaw:.2f})"131 )132133 st["index"] += 1134135136def start_driving(path=JSONL_PATH):137 stop_driving()138 records = _load_records(path)139 if not records:140 unreal.log_error(f"[orion] no records loaded from {path}")141 return142143 _state["records"] = records144 _state["index"] = 0145 _state["elapsed"] = 0.0146 _state["t0"] = None147 _state["camera"] = _get_or_spawn_camera()148 _state["tick_handle"] = unreal.register_slate_post_tick_callback(_on_tick)149 unreal.log(150 f"[orion] driving {len(records)} records from {path} -- call stop_driving() to stop early"151 )152153154def stop_driving():155 if _state["tick_handle"] is not None:156 unreal.unregister_slate_post_tick_callback(_state["tick_handle"])157 _state["tick_handle"] = None158 unreal.log("[orion] stopped driving")159160161start_driving()162163# ---- Troubleshooting --------------------------------------------------------164# - "AttributeError: module 'unreal' has no attribute 'EditorActorSubsystem'"165# or similar: older/newer UE Python API surface differs slightly by minor166# version. Try unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_all_level_actors() /167# .spawn_actor_from_class() as a fallback (deprecated but often still168# present).169# - "TypeError" from unreal.Quat(...) or .rotator(): some UE Python builds170# expose Quat as positional-only; try171# unreal.Quat(quat_ue[0], quat_ue[1], quat_ue[2], quat_ue[3]).172# - Camera doesn't visibly move: check the viewport is set to Realtime, and173# that you're looking at/through the CineCameraActor (select it, then174# View > "Pilot Actor", or press the camera icon in the World Outliner175# row for that actor).176# - Nothing prints in Output Log: confirm the log category filter isn't177# hiding LogPython messages.178

1# Part 2 - The Reconstruction Range-Check23Artifact reviewed: `orion-reconstruction-artifact.json` (`FIXTURE-orion-reconstruction-artifact`).4Read-and-reason only, per the challenge - no COLMAP or solver run. `qualification_gate.py` in this5folder is a standalone, runnable check against the artifact's own JSON that demonstrates the finding6below concretely (run it: `python qualification_gate.py ../orion-reconstruction-artifact.json`).78## (a) The defect, and how to verify it910**The reconstruction's metric scale is wrong by ~14.3%, and the artifact's own scale-correction11field falsely claims no correction was needed.**1213The artifact includes an RTK baseline cross-check - three surveyed reference distances compared14against the corresponding distances in the reconstruction:1516| pair | reference (m) | reconstructed (m) | reconstructed / reference |17|------|---------------|--------------------|-----------------------------|18| b1 | 12.40 | 10.63 | 0.8573 |19| b2 | 8.10 | 6.94 | 0.8568 |20| b3 | 20.05 | 17.19 | 0.8574 |2122All three ratios agree to within 0.03% of each other (mean 0.8571, i.e. almost exactly 6/7),23despite spanning baselines from 8m to 20m in different parts of the site. That tightness is the24signature of a single uniform multiplicative scale error, not per-point reprojection noise - noise25would scatter the ratios; a scale bug reproduces the same ratio everywhere.2627Yet `sfm_solve.metric_scale.reported_scale_factor` is recorded as `1.000` - the field meant to28record what correction the pipeline applied says "none was needed," while the baseline data sitting29in the same object shows a correction of ~1.167x was actually required. Either the scale-estimation30step (`method: estimated_from_rtk_baselines`) silently failed and left the default identity value in31place, or it computed the factor and never applied it. Either way, every downstream consumer32inherits a scene that is uniformly ~14% undersized in real-world terms: the delivered "neutral33master" and both creative derivatives will be measurably wrong wherever absolute scale matters -34placing the splat in an Unreal scene at 1:1, compositing a real object or actor into it, physics/35collision against it, or matching it to any other metric asset will all be off by the same ~14%.3637**How to verify it** (from the artifact alone, no solver needed):381. Compute `reconstructed_m / reference_m` for each baseline pair - done above; the three values39 agree to ~0.03%, confirming a uniform scale error rather than noise.402. Compare that measured ratio against `reported_scale_factor`. They should be reciprocal41 (`reported_scale_factor ≈ 1 / mean_ratio`) if the correction was computed and applied correctly.42 Here `reported_scale_factor = 1.000` while the data implies `1.167` was needed - a direct,43 falsifiable contradiction within the artifact itself, not a judgment call.443. (If the delivered scene were available to inspect, as a second independent check): measure the45 same six RTK-surveyed points in the delivered splat/Unreal import and confirm the ~14% undersize46 propagated all the way through training, not just present in the intermediate SfM solve.4748Two secondary, corroborating quality signals in the same artifact (not the primary defect, but49worth noting as further evidence this solve should never have qualified): `registration_retention`50is only 0.752 (611/812 images registered), and `reprojection_error_px` is elevated (median 2.94px,51p95 11.7px, max 41.2px) with `inlier_ratio` at 0.61. None of these alone proves the scene is52*wrong* the way the scale contradiction does - a solve can have moderate reprojection error and53still be metrically correct - but they're additional, already-computed signals that a real gate54should also have caught.5556## (b) The qualification gate that should have caught it5758The artifact's own `qualification` block shows why this shipped: `"qualified": true`,59`"gate_version": "none"`, `"reviewed_by": "auto"` - there was no real gate, just an automatic60rubber stamp, even though the RTK cross-check data needed to catch this was already sitting in the61same file. `splat_training.input_gate` (`"solve.qualification.qualified == true"`) then trusted62that stamp blindly.6364The gate that should have run instead, before `qualified` can ever be set `true`65(implemented and demonstrated in `qualification_gate.py`):66671. **Scale check (hard block).** For every RTK baseline pair, compute68 `ratio = reconstructed_m / reference_m`. Fail if `|mean(ratio) - 1.0|` exceeds a tolerance69 (2% here, informed by expected RTK survey precision) - this is a hard, falsifiable numeric70 check, not a heuristic, because the ground truth is already in the artifact.712. **Scale self-consistency check (hard block).** Fail if `reported_scale_factor` disagrees with72 `1 / mean(ratio)` by more than a small tolerance (2%). This is the specific check that catches73 *this* defect: it doesn't just verify the scale is right, it verifies the pipeline's own claim74 about what it did matches the evidence, which is what was actually broken here.753. **Ratio-spread check.** Fail if the per-pair ratios disagree with each other by more than ~1% -76 that would indicate non-uniform distortion rather than a clean scale bug, and needs a human, not77 just a scale correction.784. **Solve-quality floor (soft/secondary block).** Minimum `registration_retention` (e.g. ≥0.85),79 maximum `reprojection_error_px.p95`/`.max` (e.g. ≤2px / ≤10px), minimum `inlier_ratio`80 (e.g. ≥0.70). Every one of these is already computed and present in the artifact - the gate just81 has to actually read them instead of auto-approving.825. **No RTK data, no qualification.** If a solve has no baseline cross-check available at all,83 qualification should fail closed (cannot verify scale), not default to `true`.8485Running this gate against the actual artifact produces:8687```88this gate's verdict: FAIL89 - metric scale is off by 14.3% (mean reconstructed/reference ratio = 0.8571 ...)90 - reported_scale_factor=1.0 does not match what the baseline data actually implies ...91 - registration_retention=0.752 below minimum 0.85 (611/812 images registered)92 - reprojection_error_px.p95=11.7 exceeds 2.0px93 - reprojection_error_px.max=41.2 exceeds 10.0px94 - inlier_ratio=0.61 below minimum 0.795```9697Wired in as `splat_training.input_gate`'s actual precondition (replacing the current98`gate_version: none` / `reviewed_by: auto` stamp), this would have blocked training entirely instead99of shipping a scene that's silently ~14% off scale.100
pythonpart2-reconstruction-range-check/qualification_gate.py
1#!/usr/bin/env python32"""The qualification gate that should have run before3`sfm_solve.qualification.qualified` could be set true for4FIXTURE-orion-reconstruction-artifact (and any solve like it).56Read-and-reason artifact per the challenge -- no COLMAP/solver run here.7This is a standalone, runnable check: point it at the artifact JSON and it8reports pass/fail with reasons, using only data already present in the file.910Usage:11 python qualification_gate.py path/to/orion-reconstruction-artifact.json12"""1314import json15import sys16from dataclasses import dataclass171819@dataclass20class GateThresholds:21 # Scale: mean absolute deviation of reconstructed/reference baseline22 # ratios from 1.0. RTK survey baselines are the ground truth here, so23 # this is a hard, falsifiable check, not a heuristic.24 max_scale_error_fraction: float = 0.02 # 2%25 # Consistency across baselines: if the ratios disagree with each other26 # by more than this, it's not a clean uniform scale bug -- something27 # else (e.g. non-rigid distortion) is wrong and needs a human, not just28 # a scale correction.29 max_scale_ratio_spread: float = 0.01 # 1%30 # The pipeline's own claimed correction factor must match what the31 # baseline data actually implies, within this tolerance. This is what32 # catches "reported_scale_factor: 1.000" being wrong/unapplied even33 # when someone did compute a metric_scale block at all.34 max_reported_vs_measured_scale_disagreement: float = 0.02 # 2%3536 min_registration_retention: float = 0.8537 max_reprojection_p95_px: float = 2.038 max_reprojection_max_px: float = 10.039 min_inlier_ratio: float = 0.70404142def check_scale(sfm: dict, thresholds: GateThresholds) -> list[str]:43 failures = []44 baseline_check = sfm.get("metric_scale", {}).get("rtk_baseline_check")45 if not baseline_check or not baseline_check.get("measured_vs_reference_m"):46 failures.append(47 "no RTK baseline cross-check present -- cannot verify metric scale at all; "48 "qualification cannot be granted without one"49 )50 return failures5152 pairs = baseline_check["measured_vs_reference_m"]53 ratios = []54 for p in pairs:55 ref, recon = p["reference_m"], p["reconstructed_m"]56 if ref <= 0:57 failures.append(f"baseline {p['pair']}: non-positive reference distance {ref}")58 continue59 ratios.append(recon / ref)6061 if not ratios:62 failures.append("all baseline pairs invalid; cannot verify scale")63 return failures6465 mean_ratio = sum(ratios) / len(ratios)66 spread = max(ratios) - min(ratios)67 scale_error_fraction = abs(mean_ratio - 1.0)6869 if scale_error_fraction > thresholds.max_scale_error_fraction:70 failures.append(71 f"metric scale is off by {scale_error_fraction * 100:.1f}% "72 f"(mean reconstructed/reference ratio = {mean_ratio:.4f} across "73 f"{len(ratios)} RTK baselines; per-pair: "74 f"{[f'{r:.4f}' for r in ratios]}), exceeds the "75 f"{thresholds.max_scale_error_fraction * 100:.0f}% tolerance"76 )7778 if spread > thresholds.max_scale_ratio_spread:79 failures.append(80 f"baseline ratios disagree with each other by {spread * 100:.1f}% "81 f"(expected a single uniform scale factor if this is a plain scale bug); "82 f"exceeds {thresholds.max_scale_ratio_spread * 100:.0f}% spread tolerance -- "83 f"investigate for non-uniform distortion, not just a scale correction"84 )8586 reported = sfm["metric_scale"].get("reported_scale_factor")87 if reported is not None:88 measured_needed = 1.0 / mean_ratio89 disagreement = abs(reported - measured_needed) / measured_needed90 if disagreement > thresholds.max_reported_vs_measured_scale_disagreement:91 failures.append(92 f"reported_scale_factor={reported} does not match what the baseline data "93 f"actually implies (measured correction needed = {measured_needed:.4f}, "94 f"{disagreement * 100:.1f}% disagreement) -- the scale correction was either "95 f"never applied or computed incorrectly despite the baseline evidence being "96 f"present Requirements

What the challenge required — and where the candidate's code meets it.

Publish a coordinate-correct pose stream at >=24 Hz

The challenge asked: a fixed output clock decoupled from input jitter that holds through dropouts

Where the code delivers this

↳orion-pose-py/orion/pipeline.py 48 Hz publisher, wiring + latency trace
↳orion-pose-py/orion/fusion.py time-ordered pose / IMU / RTK fusion run
Fuse the sensors into one estimate that beats any single source

The challenge asked: a real state estimator with an observability argument, not a hand-tuned blend

Where the code delivers this

↳orion-pose-py/orion/ekf.py 15-dim error-state EKF; a pose-source bias state RTK makes observable
Coordinate-frame transform correctness (handedness, quaternion order, origin)

The challenge asked: a genuine change-of-basis (not a component relabel), verified by test

Where the code delivers this

↳orion-pose-py/orion/transform.py ENU->target transform: axis permute, handedness flip, m->cm, origin anchor
↳orion-pose-py/orion/quat.py quaternion math + reorder
↳orion-pose-py/tests/test_transform.py change-of-basis property test that catches a silent relabel
Safe degraded / last-good behavior across dropouts

The challenge asked: hold last-good, never invent fresh state from stale input, honest re-sync

Where the code delivers this

↳orion-pose-py/orion/dropout.py tracking/degraded/lost state machine, hard-cut re-sync (no smoothing)
Reject faulty observations, each with a reason

The challenge asked: specificity-ordered checks that catch the injected faults without false rejects

Where the code delivers this

↳orion-pose-py/orion/validator.py duplicate / out-of-order / stale rejection with reasons
A measured, reproducible report

The challenge asked: real measured numbers that reproduce from the same code + config

Where the code delivers this

↳orion-pose-py/report.md measured report; every number reproduces byte-for-byte on re-run
↳orion-pose-py/deliverables/orion-eval-output.jsonl his held-out eval output stream
Part 2 - catch the reconstruction defect + write a fail-closed gate

The challenge asked: prove the defect from the artifact's own numbers, then gate it before training

Where the code delivers this

↳part2-reconstruction-range-check/qualification_gate.py runnable fail-closed gate; blocks a mis-scaled solve
↳part2-reconstruction-range-check/analysis.md the 14.3% metric-scale defect, proven from 3 agreeing RTK baselines
Bonus - drive a live Unreal Engine camera + verify the readback

The challenge asked: feed the pose into the engine and check the engine's own render-space readback

Where the code delivers this

↳orion-pose-py/unreal_bridge/OrionCameraDriver.cpp C++ actor: target->Unreal remap
↳orion-pose-py/unreal_bridge/unreal-readback-log.json the engine's readback log - matched intended to 0.0 cm
